At_3CGb_.md.category_evidence: A fire-offering rite ("སྦྱིན་སྲེག་གི་ཆོ་ག") for a mantrin with samaya: deity yoga, construction of the hearth, burning substances; one of Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts. The guide files fire offerings and tantric rites under Tantras.

At_3CGc_.md.category_evidence: "ལྷ་མཆོད་པའི་རིམ་པ": a deity-offering (pūjā) rite to win siddhis, with "རྫས་སྔགས་ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན"; listed in At_3CGi_'s colophon among Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts ("ལྷ་མཆོད་པ").

At_3CGd_.md.category_evidence: A longevity practice ("ཚེ་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་ཐབས") with self-generation as the deity, a syllable visualisation and mantras ending "སྭཱ་ཧཱ"; one of Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts.

At_3CGe_.md.category_evidence: "འཆི་བ་སླུ་བ" (cheating death): a yogin's method for when death signs appear, with wind and bindu practices ("ཐིག་ལེ་འབར་འཛག"); listed among Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts.

At_3CGf_.md.category_evidence: Instruction for the moment of death ("འཆི་ཀ་མའི་བསྟན་ཆོས") that assumes empowerment, generation and completion ("སྐྱེད་རྫོགས") and samaya, with transference through "ཚངས་པའི་བུ་ག"; listed among Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts.

At_3CGg_.md.category_evidence: A cremation rite ("རོ་བསྲེག་གི་ཆོ་ག") that offers the corpse to the deities through the fire god and writes the chosen deity's heart mantra on the body; one of Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts.

At_3CGh_.md.category_evidence: A seventh-day funerary rite ("བདུན་ཚིགས་ཀྱི་ཆོ་ག") for the deceased: separating them from the executioner, ablution, deity generation and empowerment, with mantras; listed among Atiśa's thirteen mantra texts.

At_3CGi_.md.category_evidence: A tsha tsha rite performed with the pride of one's chosen deity and the mantra "སརྦ་ཀ་རི་ཧཱུཾ". The colophon names it the last of "ཏི་པཾ་ཀ་རའི་སྔགས་ལུགས་བཅུ་གསུམ".

At_3CGj_.md.category_evidence: A sādhana of Acala ("ཁྲོ་བོའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་མི་གཡོ་བ་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་ཐབས") with deity meditation and recitation, ending on "ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོའི་དངོས་གྲུབ". The guide files sādhanas under Tantras.

At_3CGk_.md.category_evidence: Self-generation, recitation and praise of Mahākāla with the curved knife ("ཡེ་ཤེས་མགོན་པོ་གྲི་གུག་ཅན་གྱི་བདག་བསྐྱེད"), ending in a linga subjugation rite. The guide files a Mahākāla sādhana (Ar_3CBf_) under Tantras.

At_3CGl_.md.category_evidence: A sādhana of the Vighna king ("བགེགས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས") with a thangka, torma, deity visualisation, mantra approach counts and activity rites; a tantric sādhana.

At_3CGm_.md.category_evidence: A sādhana of the peaceful Gaṇapati ("དཔལ་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་བདག་པོ་ཞི་བའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས") with a maṇḍala, torma, jñānasattva and samayasattva; its colophon says it rests on "དངོས་གྲུབ་འབྱུང་བའི་རྒྱུད".

At_3CGn_.md.category_evidence: The secret sādhana of Gaṇapati ("ཚོགས་ཀྱི་བདག་པོའི་གསང་བའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས") with a maṇḍala, vase, recitation and dissolution of the jñānasattva; a tantric sādhana.

At_3CGo_.md.category_evidence: A metrical praise (82% verse) describing the iconography of the wealth lord and his four ḍākinīs ("ནོར་བདག་གཙོ་འཁོར་ལྔའི་བསྟོད་པ") as wisdom-bodies. The guide files the tantric deity praise At_3CFl_ ("རྡོ་རྗེ་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མ་ལ་བསྟོད་པ") under Tantras; Liturgy is the alternative.

At_3CGp_.md.category_evidence: Orthographic verses on how to write and pronounce the ye dharmā dhāraṇī correctly: counting its 35 letters, long vowels, subscripts and stacks ("ཡིག་འབྲུ་སུམ་ཅུ་སོ་ལྔ་ལ། །འཐུག་པོ་གསུམ་དང་ལོག་པ་གསུམ"). It is a spelling and recitation guide, so the subject is language rather than doctrine; Tantras or Miscellaneous are alternatives.

At_3CGw_.md.category_evidence: A commentary on Nāgārjuna's Sūtrasamuccaya (root category: Middle Way) that arranges its meaning as "མན་ངག་གི་མདོ་རྣམ་པ་བདུན" for practice. It follows its root, though the content is close to Mind Trainings and Advices.

At_3CH8.md.category_evidence: Atiśa's instruction drawn from the sūtras on fifty dharmas that are a bodhisattva's wealth ("བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ནོར་ལྟ་བུའི་ཆོས་ནི་ལྔ་བཅུ"). The guide files Atiśa's similar bodhisattva-path works (At_3CGy_, At_3CH2, At_3CH3) under Middle Way.

At_3CHA.md.category_evidence: Atiśa's "ལས་རྣམ་པར་འབྱེད་པ" distinguishes virtuous and non-virtuous karma and their results, as practice advice ("བདག་ཉིད་ཁོ་ན་དྲན་ཕྱིར་བྲི་བར་བྱ"). It is filed with Atiśa's other path works, which the guide places under Middle Way; Mind Trainings and Advices is a close alternative.

At_3CHF.md.category_evidence: A tsha tsha rite explicitly of the Pāramitāyāna ("ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ཐེག་པའི་ཚ་ཚ་གདབ་པའི་ཆོ་ག"): it recites a dhāraṇī 21 times over clay to make stūpas and ends with a dedication prayer. It is a non-tantric recitation rite, the kind of rite the guide's Liturgy examples include; Tantras is the alternative.
